newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish cabinet meeting Tuesday, first for 8 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Turkish cabinet meeting Tuesday, first for 8 weeks.

text.p: Turkey's cabinet was to meet for the first time in eight weeks on Tuesday amid a political crisis caused by a row between the Islamist wing of the government and the secularist army, the deputy prime minister's office said.
A spokesman at Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's office told Reuters the cabinet would meet at 1700 (1400 GMT).
A scheduled ministers' meeting was postponed last Thursday amid reports Ciller had demanded Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan hand power to her to prevent the government collapsing.
Four anti-Islamist MPs from Ciller's True Path Party have resigned in recent days, reducing the government's majority on paper to only one.
But Erbakan has four more MPs than the combined opposition since two parliament seats are vacant.
Erbakan narrowly survived a censure motion in parliament last week with the help of six members of a far-right party.
